focus: Detector heuristic, false-positive surface and fixtures
answeredQuestions: What detector heuristic works (lettered or numbered option list plus a question near the end of the last assistant message, with no ask-tool call in the turn), and what is its false-positive risk on ordinary numbered steps, summaries and code blocks?
noveltyJustification: Eight findings are new analysis of an existing detector; one is a partial synthesis of which false-positive vectors survive its prose stripper.
ruledOut: Reusing isProcessQuestion as the guard filter
A pure last_assistant_message check with no tool scan

label: A question detector already exists in chat-questions.mjs: closing-paragraph question plus lettered options, with process questions skipped; the guard can reuse it.
The detector's option grammar is A-D only, so numbered, A. and Option 1: menus are invisible; enforcement needs a wider grammar.
The prose stripper removes fenced code, inline code, quotes, blockquotes, tables and headings before the question test, which is the anti-code-block defense.
Ordinary numbered steps are low risk because the option gate requires an A)-shaped marker, not a number.
Summaries are low risk while a question mark is required and no option list is printed; a summary with four A) lines is the residual intended fire.
Two false-positive vectors remain: options-only code blocks and blockquoted menus, because option extraction reads raw lines while only the question test is prose-stripped.
The no-ask-tool-call half is already implemented per runtime by the decision-capture transcript sweeps (AskUserQuestion, request_user_input, question, ask_user_question).
Claude's Stop payload carries the text but not the tool history, so the guard needs last_assistant_message plus transcript_path.
The fixture base is positive-only: ask fixtures exist for Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and Devin plus 13 detector tests, but no negative menu fixtures.

direction: Reusing isProcessQuestion as the guard filter
reason: It suppresses scope, permission, gate and shipping questions from capture, which are exactly the decisions the ask surface must carry.

direction: A pure last_assistant_message check with no tool scan
reason: It cannot distinguish a turn that asked through the tool from one that printed a menu.
